newsitem.title: UK: Bank sector leads Hong Kong stocks in London lower.
newsitem.headline: Bank sector leads Hong Kong stocks in London lower.

text.p: Hong Kong shares fell in London on Tuesday as profit-taking in the banking sector led prices lower, traders said.
Nervousness ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting also weighed on shares.

Profit-taking in the UK banking sector prompted selling in HSBC Holdings and a cautious statement by Hang Seng Bank chief executive Alexander Au that profit margins were likely to come under pressure in the second half added downward pressure.

"The rest of the market is basically unchanged although everyone is slightly defensively bid because of the FOMC meeting. I think a cut of 25 basis points in U.S. interest rates is priced in and if that's what we get the market will steady up," said a trader.
By 1410 GMT, the Hang Seng London reference index was down 51.67 points at 11,495.03.

Overnight, the Hang Seng finished 75.43 points lower at 11,546.70, with the U.S. Federal reserve's policy meeting and share placements from Henderson Land and COSCO Pacific taking the steam out of the market.
